pathway.title: Lumen Technologies, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The revenue base is shrinking faster than growth products replace it: in Q3 2026 Strategic revenue rose 10% but Legacy revenue fell 17%, so Legacy lost USD 222 million while Strategic gained USD 112 million, a loss of 1.98x the gain, and group revenue fell 12% with the Mass Markets sale. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 49; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C3; calculation C5

- The Legacy decline is broad, not confined to one channel: Legacy revenue fell in all five Business sales channels, from 12.75% in Wholesale to 26.67% in International and Other, while Strategic revenue grew in all five, led by Large Enterprise at 15.19%, so the mix shift is real but does not yet offset the decline. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C6

- Cost flexibility has protected margins but not earnings: Adjusted EBITDA excluding Special Items fell 9.15% in Q3 2026 against revenue down 12.05%, so the margin rose to 26.3% from 25.5%, and interest expense fell 40.75%, yet the net cash cost of Special Items rose to USD 912 million in nine months from USD 353 million, which the headline measure leaves out. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 16–17; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C9

- Cash conversion is the weakest dimension: free cash flow excluding Special Items of USD 1,007 million in nine months includes a USD 729 million divestiture receipt and a USD 420 million tax refund, and without them was negative USD 142 million, while operating cash flow before the change in deferred revenue was USD 980 million against capital expenditure of USD 2,717 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 58; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 16; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9

- The FY2026 outlook needs a large fourth-quarter inflow: it implies free cash flow excluding Special Items of USD 893 million to USD 1,093 million in Q4 against negative USD 76 million in Q3, and earnings less interest, capital expenditure and an implied tax refund at the outlook midpoints give about negative USD 55 million, so roughly USD 1,048 million must come from working capital and customer prepayments; the derived Q4 2025 free cash flow was negative USD 1,082 million on a reported basis. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 79–80; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12

- Leverage is lower but still high on a clean basis: total debt is 5.70x normalized Adjusted EBITDA against 6.67x at FY2025, and net debt is 5.27x, above the 5.25x revolver test level, although the covenant definition is not printed, so no breach and no headroom is inferred. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 30; calculation C2; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity is adequate and maturities are remote: USD 1,655 million of liquidity compares with USD 34 million of principal due by the end of 2027, 92.07% of principal falls due in 2031 or later, and net cash interest is guided at USD 650 million to USD 750 million, so the pressure is cash use, not refinancing. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 28, 53; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C10; calculation C14; calculation C16; calculation C19

- Capital intensity limits deleveraging: capital expenditure was 38.05% of last-twelve-month revenue, and the USD 3,200 million to USD 3,400 million guided for the next 12 months is 96.97% to 109.68% of the FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA outlook, so debt reduction from operations needs capital spending to fall or prepayments to continue. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C13

- Governance and structure add a medium risk that decides who bears stress: Level 3 Financing carries 74.22% of principal and Lumen is issuer or guarantor of 71.23%, and liability management since 2024 changed rankings, so a downside would fall unevenly across creditor classes. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17

cells.text: Digital networking services company that sells connectivity, IP, wavelength, dark fiber and conduit, edge, colocation and security services mainly to enterprise, public-sector and wholesale customers over its own and leased fiber. After the 2026-02-02 sale of its fiber-to-the-home business, its remaining Mass Markets business is mainly copper broadband and voice.

Business customers are served through five channels: Large Enterprise, Mid-Market Enterprise, Public Sector, Wholesale, and International and Other. Mass Markets serves residential and small business customers.

Revenue USD 2,715 million: Business Strategic USD 1,279 million (47.11%), Business Legacy USD 1,067 million (39.30%) and Mass Markets USD 369 million (13.59%). Strategic revenue is 54.52% of Business revenue; the company states 55%.

Service contracts with an average life of about 38 months for Business customers and 50 months for Mass Markets customers. Remaining performance obligations are USD 6.1 billion: USD 940 million for the rest of 2026, USD 2.7 billion for 2027 and USD 2.5 billion thereafter. Total deferred revenue is USD 9,258 million, including advance payments under private connectivity fabric agreements.
About 163,000 fiber on-net buildings and over 340,000 route miles of fiber at 2025-12-31, much of it owned and a substantial portion leased from other carriers; about 24,000 employees.
No single customer is more than 10% of revenue. Revenue and assets outside the United States are each below 10% of the total.

Sell private connectivity fabric solutions that monetize network assets, expand capacity through an AI backbone, manage non-core business for cash flow, and strengthen the financial position through lower costs and debt reduction. This is management language, not a documented result.

Mass Markets fiber-to-the-home business in 11 states sold to AT&T on 2026-02-02; Alkira, Inc. acquired by Level 3 Communications, LLC on 2026-07-01 for USD 485 million cash; one reportable segment from the first quarter of 2026 (two before).

Leases fiber from other carriers under arrangements that must be renewed, relies on a limited number of suppliers, and notes that some hyperscaler customers have built infrastructure that reduced their reliance on its network.

Regulated by the Federal Communications Commission and state commissions, including Universal Service Fund obligations. Lumen relinquished its Rural Digital Opportunity Fund awards in January 2026 and paid USD 99 million, so that funding ends.
Not materially affected; network operating expenses are generally higher in the second and third quarters.

runs.text: The strongest credit support is liquidity with remote maturities: cash of USD 978 million and USD 677 million of revolver availability give USD 1,655 million against USD 34 million of principal due by the end of 2027, so a cash shortfall would take time to become a refinancing problem. The second is cost flexibility, which kept the Adjusted EBITDA margin excluding Special Items at 26.3% as revenue fell 12.05%. The third is a lower interest burden, with interest expense down 40.75% in Q3 as debt fell, which leaves more of each dollar of earnings for capital spending. The fourth is a diversified customer base, with no customer above 10% of revenue and USD 6.1 billion of remaining performance obligations, which limits single-name loss. The fifth is the growth products, where Strategic revenue is 54.52% of Business revenue and rising. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 28, 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 149; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C14

The main weakness is cash flow that depends on customer prepayments and one-off receipts: free cash flow excluding Special Items was negative USD 142 million without two receipts, so a slowdown in prepayments would show up first in cash. The second is a shrinking revenue base, with Legacy revenue losing 1.98x what Strategic gains. The third is capital intensity at 38.05% of revenue, which absorbs the cash that would repay debt. The fourth is leverage of 5.70x on a normalized basis with the covenant definition not printed, which leaves headroom unproven. The fifth is governance and structure, rated medium, where repeated liability management means creditor classes would not share a downside equally. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 27; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C9; calculation C13

cells.text: Lumen Technologies, Inc., formerly named CenturyLink, Inc., a Louisiana corporation incorporated in 1968, reporting consolidated with its subsidiaries.
Common stock under LUMN, on the New York Stock Exchange until 2026-10-05 and on Nasdaq from 2026-10-06; two Qwest note series moved with it.
1,031,042,677 common shares at 2026-10-30; non-affiliate market value USD 4.4 billion at 2025-06-30; no common dividend since 2022.
KPMG LLP, Denver, Colorado; opinion on the FY2025 statements and on internal control dated 2026-02-20.
Consolidated US GAAP in USD millions; one operating segment from the first quarter of 2026, two (Business and Mass Markets) before.
In February 2026 Moody's and Fitch raised the corporate family rating and issuer default rating to B2 and B; instrument ratings range from Caa1 to Ba3 at Moody's and from B- to B+ at S&P.

Nine directors, including a non-executive chairman, and three officers (chief executive, chief financial and chief accounting) signed the FY2025 annual report on 2026-02-20; directors' independence and holdings are in the proxy statement, which is not supplied.
None named in the filings supplied; beneficial ownership is incorporated by reference to the proxy statement, which is not supplied.
United States; telecommunications and enterprise network services.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On 2026-02-02 Lumen completed the sale of its Mass Markets Fiber-to-the-Home business in 11 states to AT&T for pre-tax cash proceeds of USD 5.72 billion, subject to post-closing adjustments; the annual report gave the headline as USD 5.75 billion. Lumen applied USD 4.8 billion of the proceeds and cash on hand to repurchase USD 4,765 million of superpriority and secured debt. It recorded a net pre-tax gain of USD 569 million and USD 729 million of liabilities for contractual credits and commercial agreements with the buyer. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 28; calculation C4; calculation C14

New debt in 2026 was issued by Level 3 Financing and Qwest. Level 3 Financing issued a further USD 650 million of 8.500% Senior Notes due 2036 on 2026-01-09 and USD 1.0 billion of 7.500% Senior Notes due 2037 on 2026-05-21, using the proceeds to buy USD 607 million of second lien notes and USD 766 million of unsecured notes. On 2026-06-11 Qwest issued USD 1,002 million of 6.500% Notes due 2051 and USD 382 million of 6.750% Notes due 2052 in exchange offers; Lumen guarantees them, and substantially all restrictive covenants were removed from USD 254 million of old notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25, 27; calculation C17

Lumen entered a USD 825 million Revolving Credit Agreement on 2026-04-14, with no borrowings at 2026-09-30, and Level 3 Financing repriced its USD 2.4 billion Term Loan B-5 on 2026-05-13. On 2026-04-30 Lumen guaranteed Level 3 Financing's first lien notes and credit agreement, USD 6,825 million of secured debt, on an unsecured basis. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28; calculation C2

Level 3 Communications acquired Alkira, Inc. for USD 485 million in cash on 2026-07-01. Earlier transactions of the same kind include the 2024 transaction support agreement, the 2024 exchange offers and tender offers, and the 2025 refinancing of first lien notes and term loans; the transaction register lists each with its amounts. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 114–120

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Balance-sheet debt fell by USD 4,248 million, or 24.36%, between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30, and net debt fell by USD 4,223 million to USD 12,215 million. The cause was the 2026-02-02 sale of the Mass Markets Fiber-to-the-Home business, whose proceeds, together with cash on hand, funded the repurchase of USD 4,765 million of superpriority notes and term loans, so the deleveraging came from an asset sale and not from earnings growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 28; calculation C14; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage is distorted in both directions. Total debt was 9.00x reported EBITDA at year-end 2025 because operating income carried a USD 628 million goodwill impairment, and it is 4.67x for the last twelve months because operating income carries the USD 569 million gain on sale. Removing the gain gives 5.85x on reported EBITDA and 5.70x on the issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA, against 6.67x on that measure at year-end 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 14; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C6; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Underlying earnings fell while debt fell: normalised last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,316 million is USD 297 million below the USD 2,613 million of FY2025, so lower earnings offset part of the debt reduction. Revenue fell 5.39% in FY2025 and the sold business no longer contributes, which is why the normalised leverage of 5.70x is the fairer starting point.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C18; calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is the outlook reiterated on 2026-11-04 for FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA excluding Special Items of USD 3.1 billion to USD 3.3 billion, against USD 2,366 million for the first nine months of 2026 on that basis, together with lower cash interest and the roughly USD 1 billion of annual Mass Markets fiber capital expenditure that leaves with the sold business. That measure is not the one used above, and the view wins only if fourth-quarter free cash flow excluding Special Items reaches the USD 893 million to USD 1,093 million the outlook implies, against negative USD 76 million in Q3 2026; it loses if the fourth quarter repeats the third.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest paid fell from USD 1,219 million in FY2025 to USD 840 million over the last twelve months as debt was repaid, lifting reported EBITDA cover from 1.59x to 3.36x; without the gain on sale, cover is 2.68x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 79–80; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; calculation C6; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow of USD 2,812 million in the first nine months of 2026 is not a clean measure of the business: it includes USD 729 million of divestiture proceeds classified as operating and a USD 1,832 million rise in deferred revenue. The filing does not say how much of the 729 sits inside the deferred revenue line, so the two are not added. After capital expenditure of USD 2,717 million, free cash flow was USD 95 million, against USD 1,453 million a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Q3 2026 alone was negative: operating cash flow of USD 518 million did not cover capital expenditure of USD 872 million, so free cash flow was negative USD 354 million. Capital expenditure absorbed 38.05% of last-twelve-month revenue against 35.21% in FY2025, and management expects USD 3.2 billion to USD 3.4 billion over the next twelve months, so free cash flow depends on customer prepayments continuing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C17; calculation C6; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was USD 1,655 million: USD 978 million of cash and USD 677 million of availability under the USD 825 million revolving credit facility after USD 148 million of undrawn letters of credit. USD 92 million of the cash is held outside the United States.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 52, 53, 57; calculation C11; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt due by the end of 2027 is only USD 34 million, the revolving facility matures on 2029-04-14, and 92.07% of principal falls due in 2031 or later, so near-term refinancing risk is small and the exposure is to the long-dated stack. The pressure on liquidity is cash use, not maturities: capital expenditure and the sign of free cash flow decide how long the cash and the revolver last.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deferred revenue, which funds operations without interest, rose to USD 9,258 million at 2026-09-30 from USD 7,411 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 4,594 million at 2024-12-31. The filing says advance payments under Private Connectivity Fabric agreements have historically increased operating cash flow and deferred revenue, vary by quarter and are applied to network expansion, which raises capital expenditure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit implication is that reported operating cash flow rests on prepayments that can slow while the obligation to deliver the network capacity and the related capital expenditure remain. The float is not debt and is not in the debt figures, but it is a liability that must be served; the backlog figure of USD 6.1 billion excludes contracts classified as leasing arrangements, so it should not be read as covering the whole balance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: One event after 2026-09-30 is disclosed, the 2026-10-06 transfer of the common stock and two Qwest note series to Nasdaq; it changes neither debt nor cash, so no figure is adjusted for it. Events after the 2025-12-31 balance sheet that change net debt are kept out of the year-end figures and listed separately: the divestiture cash of USD 5,706 million and the USD 470 million paid for Alkira net of cash acquired. The 2026-09-30 balance sheet already reflects both.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14, 15; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The divestiture carries several figures for one event: pre-tax cash proceeds of USD 5.72 billion before post-closing adjustments, USD 4,977 million classified as investing cash flow, USD 729 million classified as operating cash flow for contractual credits and commercial agreements, and a USD 569 million net gain. The cash flow figures serve the net debt effect because they are cash received; the headline is not used because it is rounded and before adjustments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA is not printed in the statements. Reported EBITDA is calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, so impairments and gains stay inside it. The issuer's Adjusted EBITDA adds back goodwill impairment and stock-based compensation but, unlike its Adjusted EBITDA excluding Special Items, keeps one-off gains and costs; only the second is the issuer's headline and it is not available for FY2025 because no fourth-quarter release was supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 149; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation C1; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The debt note foots to the balance sheet and the maturity ladder, and the Q3 2026 release ties to the quarterly report on revenue, net loss and cash. Segment reporting changed from two segments to one in 2026 and revenue categories were relabelled, so segment history comes from the annual report and is not spliced with 2026 category data. A new finance system went live in Q4 2025 and was substantially completed in Q3 2026; the auditor reported evidence over it as a critical audit matter, so the statements were prepared while controls were changing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The three points are not on the same earnings quality: FY2025 EBITDA carries a goodwill impairment and the last twelve months carry a gain on sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cover is on cash interest paid rather than interest expense, and the last-twelve-month point includes the gain on sale in EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Undrawn committed facilities are net of letters of credit, and the 2024-12-31 availability is stated by the filing as approximate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The last row groups all principal due in 2031 and thereafter, so it is not a single year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The three years include divested businesses and are not like-for-like with 2026, and Adjusted EBITDA keeps one-off gains and costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No legal ranking across Lumen Technologies, Level 3 Financing and Qwest is stated, so no stack is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The bridge covers FY2025 only and adds back no gain or one-off cost because the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA does not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each row below works a figure used in the tables or the findings from the printed inputs; the ratio rows themselves are in the calculation register.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA excluding Special Items, the issuer's headline measure, is not available for FY2025 or FY2024 because no fourth-quarter or annual release was supplied; this restricts a like-for-like last-twelve-month leverage on that basis, and the action that would close it is the fourth-quarter 2025 results release. Severity: High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA is a derived figure, not printed by the issuer, and it keeps a USD 628 million goodwill impairment in FY2025 and a USD 569 million gain on sale in the last twelve months; this restricts the reported leverage ratios to a labelled, unadjusted reading, and the normalised rows partly close it. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant ratio definitions, the covenant EBITDA and the reported covenant ratios are not printed in any source, so no headroom against the 5.25x total net leverage and 2.00x interest coverage tests is calculated; the action is the revolving credit agreement and the latest compliance certificate. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Carrying value by instrument and by seniority is not disclosed, so senior secured debt to EBITDA and the facility-level carrying values are Not calculable; the debt table gives principal by line and one aggregate financing cost adjustment. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No legal ranking across Lumen, Level 3 Financing and Qwest debt is stated, so the debt stack table is left without a ranked stack; the action is the security and intercreditor documents. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Funds from operations is not defined in any source, so FFO to debt is Not calculable; the issuer's Unlevered Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow are the nearest measures and are not substitutes. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A dash in a filing is carried as Not supplied and never as zero: net loss on sale of businesses in FY2025, 9M 2025 and Q3 2025, goodwill impairment in FY2024, 9M 2026, Q3 2025 and Q3 2026, goodwill at 2025-12-31 and the other dash lines of the statements; these restrict nothing, because the statements foot without them. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lines that the quarterly reports do not print separately are Not supplied for the interim columns: impairment of long-lived assets, debt modification costs, gain on sale of investment, unrealized loss on investments, revolving line of credit and dividends paid; the totals foot, and the lines affect no ratio. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Assets held for sale and liabilities held for sale are not separated in the FY2023 balance sheet, because the FY2024 report prints a single Other line; the FY2023 other current assets figure therefore includes any such assets. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The FY2024 and FY2025 segment data use two segments and the Grow, Nurture, Harvest and Other categories, and 2026 uses one segment and Strategic and Legacy; the release channel revenue for Q3 2025 and Q3 2026 is a customer-group view, and segment adjusted EBITDA is not stated for 2026. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The release states Q4 2025 revenue by channel only, so Q4 2025 statements and the discrete fourth-quarter cash flow are not supplied; no quarterly series is built for 2025 other than Q3. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The KPI dashboard cells marked Not supplied are periods for which the issuer states no value for that measure; Network-as-a-Service customers is stated only as more than 4,000. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The USD 5.72 billion headline divestiture proceeds are rounded and before post-closing adjustments, and the cash taxes paid on the gain are not netted in the post-balance-sheet table; the pro forma leverage divides by unchanged FY2025 EBITDA and so overstates leverage after the sale. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2024-12-31 revolver availability is stated by the issuer as approximate, and the fiscal-year balance sheet for 2023 supports no liquidity figure; the liquidity table starts at 2024-12-31. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The finance system change, with an auditor critical audit matter over its implementation, means the FY2025 and 2026 statements were prepared while controls were changing; this lowers reliance on small line-level differences and restricts nothing in the totals. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Lumen Technologies, Inc. (issuer id lumn-18926), as of 2026-11-18. Pathway: credit snapshot, limited in this run to the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit modules. Scope: the business, transactions, ownership, control, debt structure by borrowing group, governance and creditor-treatment behavior of the issuer through the quarter ended 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors face medium governance and structure risk at Lumen: debt sits in four borrowing groups with different guarantees and liability management since 2024 changed rankings, but no sponsor is named and no common dividend has been paid since 2022.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 Mass Markets sale and USD 4,765 million of debt repurchases cut balance-sheet debt from USD 17,441 million at year-end 2025 to USD 13,193 million, and Lumen is now issuer or guarantor of 71.23% of debt principal. Executed financing documents are not supplied, so lien, guarantee-release and covenant terms are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 28; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C22; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership risk is low on the evidence but unproven: no sponsor or controlling holder is named, no common dividend has been paid since 2022 and most of the sale proceeds repaid debt, yet the proxy statement that would show large holders and director independence is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt is concentrated in the Level 3 group, so recovery and refinancing turn on Level 3's assets and cash flow: Level 3 Financing carries 74.22% of debt principal, Qwest Corporation 13.00%, Lumen itself 9.67% and Qwest Capital Funding 1.24%, and Level 3 Parent's revenue from outside affiliates was 56.85% of group revenue in nine months 2026 before eliminations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23, 61; calculation C1; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Guarantees now run to the parent: Lumen is issuer or guarantor of 71.23% of debt principal against the 9.67% that is its own notes, so holders of Lumen's unsecured notes share the parent's assets with guaranteed Level 3 Financing and Qwest creditors. The filings say the guarantees simplify reporting and do not discuss the effect on Lumen's own noteholders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 26, 30; calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liability management is a pattern, not a single event, and it re-ranked claims each time. The 2024 transaction support agreement exchanged USD 10,244 million and repaid USD 2,258 million of debt into superpriority, first lien and second lien instruments, the 2024 exchange offers swapped USD 848 million of unsecured notes for USD 788 million of secured notes, second lien notes later became unsecured, and the 2026 Qwest exchange removed covenants from USD 254 million of notes that stayed out. The filings do not say what holders outside each deal received, so the size of the value transfer is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 118–120, 125; 10-Q_2026-03-31_lumn-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 24–25; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital allocation favors creditors on balance. USD 4,765 million of superpriority and secured debt was repurchased on 2026-02-02, the 2025 refinancings replaced the highest-coupon first lien notes with lower-coupon notes, and the revolver has no borrowings. The cost is that the sale also removed earnings, and USD 729 million of the cash was classified as operating cash flow against credits owed to the buyer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business mix is improving but not fast enough to offset what was sold or is declining: Strategic revenue rose 10% in Q3 2026, Legacy revenue fell 17% and Mass Markets revenue fell 42%, leaving group revenue 12% lower, and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reporting is sound at group level but thinner for creditors of Level 3 and Qwest. KPMG LLP audited the FY2025 statements and internal control was effective, although the auditor flagged the new finance system as a critical audit matter, and Level 3 Parent and Qwest have stopped separate filings, so those creditors now rely on summaries inside Lumen's reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Alkira purchase adds little asset cover: Level 3 Communications paid USD 485 million in cash on 2026-07-01 and 99.18% of the price is goodwill and intangible assets. It is small against debt and cash-funded, so it does not signal a debt-funded roll-up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Protection for tax losses ends in late 2026: the rights agreement that protects USD 982 million of federal tax losses is scheduled to lapse, after which a large share purchase could limit use of the losses. Change of control offers at 101% protect holders of Lumen and Level 3 Financing notes, but the filing describes no such offer for Qwest's older notes and does not describe the terms of the new Qwest notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for lower risk is that owners have not taken value out and financial policy has turned toward creditors. USD 4,765 million of superpriority and secured debt was repaid from sale proceeds and cash, no common dividend has been paid since 2022, Moody's and Fitch each raised the corporate rating in February 2026, and liquidity of USD 1,655 million compares with USD 34 million of principal due by the end of 2027, with 92.07% of principal due in 2031 or later.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 28, 53, 58; calculation C4; calculation C9; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management's own record points the other way on growth: it says Strategic sales rose 30% year on year and cumulative signed private connectivity fabric agreements exceed USD 13.5 billion. These are company statements, the contracts are not supplied and the cash arrives as advance payments, so they do not by themselves lower the risk level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to high risk on executed documents showing wide capacity for added debt, liens, investments or asset transfers outside the guarantor groups, evidence that holders outside the 2024 and 2026 exchanges lost priority or guarantees, a further exchange with covenant removal, or a controlling holder emerging after the rights agreement lapses. It would move to low risk if the documents show tight restrictions, a full year passes without another exchange or covenant removal, and deleveraging continues from earnings rather than asset sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the reading that no sponsor or controlling holder exists rests on silence; a large holder or a board with limited independence would move the risk level up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed indentures and credit agreements are not supplied, so the lien, guarantee-release and capacity findings rest on the quarterly report summaries; different release or priority terms would change the medium rating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings do not say what holders outside each exchange received or how many took part, so the finding that rankings changed cannot be sized; a poor outcome for those holders would move the rating toward high.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Level 3 Parent and Qwest figures are summarized before eliminations, so their shares of group revenue and debt are indicative and could overstate the Level 3 concentration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Private connectivity fabric terms and customer identities are not supplied and the signed-agreement total is management's, so the view of cash-flow quality could be wrong in either direction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Nothing dated after 2026-11-04 is covered, so a financing, rating action or ownership filing in the 14 days to the as-of date could change the medium rating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-02-02 Lumen completed the sale of its Mass Markets Fiber-to-the-Home business in 11 states to AT&T for pre-tax cash proceeds of USD 5.72 billion, subject to post-closing adjustments; the annual report gave the headline as USD 5.75 billion. Lumen applied USD 4.8 billion of the proceeds and cash on hand to repurchase USD 4,765 million of superpriority and secured debt. It recorded a net pre-tax gain of USD 569 million and USD 729 million of liabilities for contractual credits and commercial agreements with the buyer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 28; calculation C4; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt in 2026 was issued by Level 3 Financing and Qwest. Level 3 Financing issued a further USD 650 million of 8.500% Senior Notes due 2036 on 2026-01-09 and USD 1.0 billion of 7.500% Senior Notes due 2037 on 2026-05-21, using the proceeds to buy USD 607 million of second lien notes and USD 766 million of unsecured notes. On 2026-06-11 Qwest issued USD 1,002 million of 6.500% Notes due 2051 and USD 382 million of 6.750% Notes due 2052 in exchange offers; Lumen guarantees them, and substantially all restrictive covenants were removed from USD 254 million of old notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lumen entered a USD 825 million Revolving Credit Agreement on 2026-04-14, with no borrowings at 2026-09-30, and Level 3 Financing repriced its USD 2.4 billion Term Loan B-5 on 2026-05-13. On 2026-04-30 Lumen guaranteed Level 3 Financing's first lien notes and credit agreement, USD 6,825 million of secured debt, on an unsecured basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Level 3 Communications acquired Alkira, Inc. for USD 485 million in cash on 2026-07-01. Earlier transactions of the same kind include the 2024 transaction support agreement, the 2024 exchange offers and tender offers, and the 2025 refinancing of first lien notes and term loans; the transaction register lists each with its amounts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by repeated liability management that re-ranked claims and by debt spread across guarantor groups, because holders' positions depend on whether they took part and which guarantee they hold, which implies class-specific loss and refinancing risk. Countervailing evidence is the absence of distributions or related-party fees, the repayment of USD 4,765 million of senior debt from sale proceeds and the February 2026 rating upgrades. Further analysis requires the proxy statement and the executed financing documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Lumen Technologies, Inc. (issuer id lumn-18926), as of 2026-11-18. Pathway: credit snapshot, limited in this run to the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit modules. Scope: the issuer's overall fundamental credit profile through the quarter ended 2026-09-30, its strongest support, weakest dimension and primary downside path, in USD millions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lumen's fundamental credit profile is weak on cash flow and adequate on liquidity: the 2026 asset sale cut debt, but free cash flow depends on customer prepayments and one-off receipts, so creditors rely on Strategic growth and prepayments continuing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 58; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C7; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt to normalized Adjusted EBITDA is 5.70x, and free cash flow excluding Special Items would have been negative USD 142 million in the first nine months without a USD 729 million divestiture receipt and a USD 420 million tax refund. Liquidity of USD 1,655 million and USD 34 million of debt due by the end of 2027 give time, but the outlook needs a large fourth-quarter working-capital inflow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 28, 53; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 16; calculation C2; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C14; calculation C16; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The revenue base is shrinking faster than growth products replace it: in Q3 2026 Strategic revenue rose 10% but Legacy revenue fell 17%, so Legacy lost USD 222 million while Strategic gained USD 112 million, a loss of 1.98x the gain, and group revenue fell 12% with the Mass Markets sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 49; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C3; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Legacy decline is broad, not confined to one channel: Legacy revenue fell in all five Business sales channels, from 12.75% in Wholesale to 26.67% in International and Other, while Strategic revenue grew in all five, led by Large Enterprise at 15.19%, so the mix shift is real but does not yet offset the decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cost flexibility has protected margins but not earnings: Adjusted EBITDA excluding Special Items fell 9.15% in Q3 2026 against revenue down 12.05%, so the margin rose to 26.3% from 25.5%, and interest expense fell 40.75%, yet the net cash cost of Special Items rose to USD 912 million in nine months from USD 353 million, which the headline measure leaves out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 16–17; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash conversion is the weakest dimension: free cash flow excluding Special Items of USD 1,007 million in nine months includes a USD 729 million divestiture receipt and a USD 420 million tax refund, and without them was negative USD 142 million, while operating cash flow before the change in deferred revenue was USD 980 million against capital expenditure of USD 2,717 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 58; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 16; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The FY2026 outlook needs a large fourth-quarter inflow: it implies free cash flow excluding Special Items of USD 893 million to USD 1,093 million in Q4 against negative USD 76 million in Q3, and earnings less interest, capital expenditure and an implied tax refund at the outlook midpoints give about negative USD 55 million, so roughly USD 1,048 million must come from working capital and customer prepayments; the derived Q4 2025 free cash flow was negative USD 1,082 million on a reported basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 79–80; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is lower but still high on a clean basis: total debt is 5.70x normalized Adjusted EBITDA against 6.67x at FY2025, and net debt is 5.27x, above the 5.25x revolver test level, although the covenant definition is not printed, so no breach and no headroom is inferred.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 30; calculation C2; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate and maturities are remote: USD 1,655 million of liquidity compares with USD 34 million of principal due by the end of 2027, 92.07% of principal falls due in 2031 or later, and net cash interest is guided at USD 650 million to USD 750 million, so the pressure is cash use, not refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 28, 53; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C10; calculation C14; calculation C16; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital intensity limits deleveraging: capital expenditure was 38.05% of last-twelve-month revenue, and the USD 3,200 million to USD 3,400 million guided for the next 12 months is 96.97% to 109.68% of the FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA outlook, so debt reduction from operations needs capital spending to fall or prepayments to continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance and structure add a medium risk that decides who bears stress: Level 3 Financing carries 74.22% of principal and Lumen is issuer or guarantor of 71.23%, and liability management since 2024 changed rankings, so a downside would fall unevenly across creditor classes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is momentum and management's outlook. Strategic revenue is 54.52% of Business revenue, up 7.00 percentage points in a year, margins are rising, interest expense fell 40.75% in Q3, Moody's and Fitch raised their ratings in February 2026, and management reiterated FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA excluding Special Items of USD 3,100 million to USD 3,300 million with free cash flow of USD 1,900 million to USD 2,100 million. If fourth-quarter free cash flow reaches the implied USD 893 million to USD 1,093 million, cash flow stability would move from weak toward average.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 3; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The outlook may include or exclude USD 321 million of cash taxes paid on the divestiture, which would lower the implied fourth-quarter figure to USD 572 million to USD 772 million, and Q3 Strategic revenue was 0.78% below Q2, so the improvement is not yet visible in the sequence of results.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 16; calculation C5; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would worsen if fourth-quarter free cash flow repeats the third quarter, if the change in deferred revenue keeps shrinking from the 25.77% fall seen in nine months, if Strategic growth stays below the Legacy decline into 2027, or if the covenant definition shows little room against the 5.25x test. It would improve if prepayments hold while capital spending falls to the guided range, and if the covenant definition shows ample room.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 54; calculation C2; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant EBITDA definition and the reported covenant ratios are not printed, so the 5.27x net leverage computed here is not a covenant ratio and the conclusion on headroom cannot be drawn either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Adjusted EBITDA excluding Special Items is not supplied for FY2025 or the last twelve months, so the margin and earnings trend on the issuer's headline measure covers only Q3 and nine months, and the leverage view rests on a measure that keeps Special Items costs in.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Whether the outlook's free cash flow includes the USD 321 million of divestiture taxes is not stated, so the implied fourth-quarter inflow could be USD 321 million smaller, which would soften the finding that the outlook is demanding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filing does not say how much of the USD 729 million divestiture receipt sits in the change in deferred revenue, so operating cash flow before that change is shown without adding the two, and the underlying cash flow could be better or worse than shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer or market data is supplied, so the business profile is judged against the issuer's own history and not against typical leveraged issuers, and the weak and adequate labels are absolute reads.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The outlook is a one-year range and the medium-term view rests on a single management statement about returning to Business revenue growth in 2028, so conclusions beyond 2027 are directional only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest credit support is liquidity with remote maturities: cash of USD 978 million and USD 677 million of revolver availability give USD 1,655 million against USD 34 million of principal due by the end of 2027, so a cash shortfall would take time to become a refinancing problem. The second is cost flexibility, which kept the Adjusted EBITDA margin excluding Special Items at 26.3% as revenue fell 12.05%. The third is a lower interest burden, with interest expense down 40.75% in Q3 as debt fell, which leaves more of each dollar of earnings for capital spending. The fourth is a diversified customer base, with no customer above 10% of revenue and USD 6.1 billion of remaining performance obligations, which limits single-name loss. The fifth is the growth products, where Strategic revenue is 54.52% of Business revenue and rising.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 28, 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 149; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weakness is cash flow that depends on customer prepayments and one-off receipts: free cash flow excluding Special Items was negative USD 142 million without two receipts, so a slowdown in prepayments would show up first in cash. The second is a shrinking revenue base, with Legacy revenue losing 1.98x what Strategic gains. The third is capital intensity at 38.05% of revenue, which absorbs the cash that would repay debt. The fourth is leverage of 5.70x on a normalized basis with the covenant definition not printed, which leaves headroom unproven. The fifth is governance and structure, rated medium, where repeated liability management means creditor classes would not share a downside equally.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 27; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C9; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lumen sells enterprise, public-sector and wholesale network services over a large owned and leased fiber network, and the business is now one reportable segment after the 2026-02-02 sale of its fiber-to-the-home operations. Service contracts average about 38 months for Business customers, USD 6.1 billion of performance obligations is contracted, and no customer is above 10% of revenue, so cash-flow visibility is reasonable through 2027 and concentration is low. The weakness is that Legacy revenue, 39.30% of Q3 revenue, is in decline and Mass Markets, 13.59%, is mainly copper broadband and voice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lumen is a widely held public holding company with no sponsor named, so the owner-extraction risk is low, and the common dividend was discontinued in 2022. Debt sits in four borrowing groups, 74.22% at Level 3 Financing, and Lumen is issuer or guarantor of 71.23% of principal, so recovery and refinancing depend on entity lines; Business & governance rates governance and sponsor risk as medium because of repeated liability management that changed rankings. The proxy statement and executed financing documents are not supplied, so concentration of holders and legal capacity are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is largely recurring and contracted but structurally declining in the legacy part. In Q3 2026 Strategic revenue was USD 1,279 million, up 10%, and fell 0.78% from Q2, while Legacy revenue was USD 1,067 million, down 17%, and fell 7.62% from Q2, so the mix is shifting but the sequential Strategic line is flat. Legacy products are voice, private line and traditional data services that customers move to alternatives, and a 7.00 percentage point rise in Strategic share of Business revenue in a year means the decline in Legacy sets the pace of group revenue. The credit implication is that revenue visibility is adequate but total revenue falls until Strategic gains exceed Legacy losses, and the 2028 return to Business growth is a management statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 21, 49; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 3; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs have fallen as fast as revenue: cost of services fell 15.76% and selling, general and administrative expense 5.43% in Q3 2026, together 12.38% against revenue down 12.05%, which kept the Adjusted EBITDA margin excluding Special Items at 26.3% against 25.5% and 28.1% against 27.7% over nine months. The sold business carried network cost, so part of the fall is the sale and not savings, and the company says it is managing vendor cost increases and dis-synergies from the divestitures. Margins can be defended under this pace of volume decline, but absolute earnings fall about as fast as revenue, and the net cash cost of Special Items, USD 912 million in nine months, is outside the headline margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 48; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings convert poorly into free cash flow. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 2,812 million is made of USD 466 million of earnings after non-cash items and USD 2,346 million of working capital and other items, led by a USD 1,832 million rise in deferred revenue and USD 875 million of accrued taxes, and capital expenditure of USD 2,717 million absorbs it. Capital expenditure is 38.05% of last-twelve-month revenue and guided at USD 3,200 million to USD 3,400 million, which is 96.97% to 109.68% of the Adjusted EBITDA outlook, partly funded by customer advance payments that are applied to network projects. The company expects the sale to cut Mass Markets fiber capital expenditure by about USD 1 billion a year, which helps, but maintenance versus growth spending is not split, so flexibility over the maturity wall is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 54, 55; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C7; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest paid fell to USD 840 million over the last twelve months from USD 1,219 million in FY2025, and is guided at USD 650 million to USD 750 million, which is the one clear cash-flow tailwind from the debt reduction. Claims outside the debt figure include net pension and retiree medical obligations of USD 1,904 million, operating lease liabilities of USD 1,379 million at 2025-12-31 and a litigation accrual of USD 50 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_lumn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 111; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C19; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry and substitution are high: competitors include global providers, hyperscalers, cable and wireless companies, and some hyperscaler customers have built infrastructure that reduced their reliance on Lumen's network, which could pressure Wholesale and Legacy revenue; buyer power is high for large enterprise and carrier customers on contracts of about 38 months; supplier power is moderate because Lumen relies on a limited number of equipment suppliers and leases part of its fiber from other carriers. New entrants are limited by capital intensity, but hyperscaler self-build is the main threat to volumes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation matters to credit through universal service funding, which Lumen gave up by relinquishing its Rural Digital Opportunity Fund awards for USD 99 million, and through a federal investigation of Huawei equipment in its networks and legacy lead-sheathed cable suits, which are contingent and carry a litigation accrual of USD 50 million. The credit-translated strengths are liquidity, cost flexibility and a diversified customer base; the weaknesses are cash conversion, shrinking revenue and capital intensity; the opportunities are AI-driven demand for private connectivity and network-as-a-service, which management says has more than 4,000 customers; the threats are hyperscaler self-build, prepayment slowdown and a further liability management round.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine dimensions the profile is weak on free cash flow stability and average elsewhere. Scale and market position are average, with last-twelve-month revenue of USD 11,460 million but a shrinking base. Competitive advantage is average, resting on the network and private connectivity contracts against hyperscaler self-build. Business diversification is average, with no customer above 10% and five sales channels but a Legacy decline in all of them. Cost and capex flexibility is average, since costs have flexed while capital expenditure is large and its maintenance share is not stated. Margin stability is average, with margins rising while earnings fall. Free cash flow stability is weak, because free cash flow depends on prepayments and one-off receipts. Ability to refinance is average, with ratings of B2 and B, frequent refinancings and remote maturities. Liquidity is adequate at USD 1,655 million. Financial policy and governance are average, with no dividend and no sponsor but a record of liability management.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 27, 58; calculation C2; calculation C9; calculation C14; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are liquidity, remote maturities, cost flexibility and a lower interest burden; the main constraints are cash conversion, capital intensity and leverage of 5.70x on a normalized basis; the trend is lower debt and lower earnings together; and the key missing datapoints are the covenant definition, prepayment terms and the maintenance share of capital expenditure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C13; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the company guides FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA excluding Special Items to USD 3,100 million to USD 3,300 million, which implies USD 734 million to USD 934 million in Q4 against USD 715 million in Q3, and free cash flow of USD 1,900 million to USD 2,100 million, which depends on a fourth-quarter inflow. Tailwinds are lower interest cost, about USD 1 billion a year less Mass Markets fiber capital expenditure, and demand for AI-related connectivity; headwinds are Legacy decline, copper decommissioning costs that management plans to accelerate in four states, Special Items net cash costs, and customers building their own networks. Over three to five years management states a return to Business revenue growth in 2028, which is not supported by a forecast in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_lumnq320268-kexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lumn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C9; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside starts with a slowdown in customer prepayments while Legacy decline continues. The change in deferred revenue has already fallen 25.77% in nine months, and operating cash flow before it is USD 980 million against capital expenditure of USD 2,717 million, so a further fall in prepayments cuts operating cash flow directly while contracted network builds and the guided USD 3,200 million to USD 3,400 million of capital expenditure keep cash out. At the guidance midpoints earnings less interest and capital expenditure is negative USD 800 million a year, before working capital, prepayments, taxes and Special Items, so liquidity of USD 1,655 million would last about 2.07 years, or 1.68 years at the last-twelve-month rate, before Special Items cash costs, and a further 9.15% fall in normalized Adjusted EBITDA would take net leverage to 5.81x against a 5.25x revolver test whose definition is not printed.

fields.value: Management can respond by deferring capital expenditure, which depends on contracted builds, and by cost cuts, which have kept margins stable, and the near-term maturity profile does not force a refinancing, so resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 unless revolver access is lost on a covenant breach. The observable triggers are Q4 free cash flow, the change in deferred revenue, Strategic revenue against the Legacy decline, and any change in the covenant compliance statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Lumen presents an adequate business profile supported by liquidity, cost flexibility, a diversified customer base and a lower interest burden, but credit quality is constrained by weak cash conversion, a shrinking revenue base and capital intensity. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow depends on customer prepayments and one-off receipts. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Q4 free cash flow, the pace of Strategic growth and ratings of B2 and B, as maturities are remote. The primary downside path is a slowdown in prepayments with Legacy decline continuing, which would turn free cash flow negative and use liquidity. Further analysis would require the covenant definition, prepayment contract terms, the maintenance share of capital expenditure and peer data. Top risk: free cash flow that relies on customer prepayments and one-off receipts.
